author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Verify a graphics fix across PS2 regions and revisions
summary: Treat each serial and executable CRC as an independent target, establish clean baselines, apply the fix only where its metadata matches, and prove that another region does not inherit unnecessary or unsafe settings.
heroAlt: Official PCSX2 per-game options interface representing serial-specific patches and fixes

sourceLabels.pcsx2-patches: Official serial and CRC patch records

blocks.text: Name each executable before comparing output

PAL, NTSC-U, NTSC-J, rereleases, and language revisions can use different executable layouts, frame rates, patches, and built-in fixes. Title text is not a safe identity. Record disc serial, region, revision, executable CRC where available, personal image hash, and profile ID for every copy before applying a graphics correction.
Do not rename a patch or profile to make it load on another region. A mismatched memory address can change unrelated logic or create a crash that has nothing to do with the visual fault.

items: Legally owned and independently verified images for each tested release.
Serial, region, revision, CRC, and private SHA-256 inventory.
The same scene reached through normal in-game saves.
Clean per-game profiles with automatic fixes recorded.
Official metadata for the proposed correction.

blocks.text: Apply the correction only to its declared target

items: 1. Cold-boot each region at safe defaults and capture the same visual checkpoint.
2. Record whether the fault actually exists in every executable.
3. Match the official fix metadata to the target serial and CRC.
4. Enable the correction for that release only and replay the checkpoint.
5. Leave the non-target region at defaults, then verify it did not inherit a copied profile.
6. Compare timing-sensitive output separately when PAL and NTSC frame behavior differs.
7. Test a second scene on each release for side effects.
8. Document minimum settings per region instead of declaring one universal fix.

blocks.text: A port can change code addresses, rendering passes, timing, and even assets. One region may already include a developer fix or require a different patch. Independent baselines prevent a correction from spreading solely because two library entries share a translated title. Preserve the clean screenshot and settings indicator for every release, because a visually similar fault can originate in a different pass and require a different minimum correction.
Every executable should carry only evidence-backed changes.

items: The target serial and CRC match the correction metadata.
The affected scene is repaired in the intended release.
A second region remains on its own clean profile.
Timing, FMV, HUD, and later scenes do not regress.
Library refresh keeps profiles attached to the correct identities.
CRC or revision is unknown: keep the fix disabled until identity is resolved.
Another region crashes after profile copying: remove the foreign settings immediately.
The fault differs between releases: write separate diagnoses.
Renaming files changes profile attachment: repair library identity before graphics work.

blocks.text: Disable the correction on the wrong serial, delete its copied override, and cold-boot the clean checkpoint. Preserve the verified target profile separately and label it with serial, CRC, emulator version, and test date.

Two discs with the same language can still have different serials or revisions, while multilingual releases can share an executable. Use technical identity rather than storefront name or displayed language.
